name: Drivers and the Miniscript
oneLine: Five half-second behavior clusters - Be Perfect, Please Others, Try Hard, Be Strong, Hurry Up - that open a miniature replay of the whole life-script, running in seconds instead of years.
whatYouDid: You read Lucia's Be Perfect tells off the page - the self-correcting parenthesis, the finger count, the eyes checking an invisible ceiling - the same way Kahler taught people to spot drivers in real time.

fromBook.quote: The five drivers are the functional manifestations of not-OK (structural) counterscripts.

expand.definition: A driver only lasts half a second to a few seconds. If the person can't sustain it long enough to satisfy their internal Parent, the miniscript moves them into a 'stopper,' 'blamer,' or 'despairer' position - a script payoff rehearsed in miniature.
expand.otherFraming: What looks like diligence (Be Perfect), kindness (Please Others), or toughness (Be Strong) in someone's personality is, in Kahler's model, conditional OKness in disguise - 'I'm OK as long as I...' - which is exactly why drivers get mistaken for virtues.
expand.tryThisToday: Catch your own primary driver once today at the half-second level - the exact gesture or phrase - and swap in its allower (for example, Be Perfect becomes 'you're good enough as you are') on purpose.
